name: Zoe Diaz

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Walk me through a workday.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43, have a bachelor's degree and manage five credit officers inside a large company. I've done it for seven years and am solidly average; mornings are unpaid invoice lists, bank receipts and calls with customers who say they paid half already. I use AI now and then to simplify a reminder, never to decide a disputed balance. I like getting a payment plan both sides can keep and hate a demand sent before a receipt is posted.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is the picture at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works full time at a vocational school and our two children are in school too. We have a mortgage, about three months of expenses saved and my pay is typical for a credit manager; there are a few similar offices nearby. I want staff and customers to be able to challenge a wrong number, whoever made it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the credit team that a better reminder letter is useful if it stops a needless second call. A customer who owes money still needs to know exactly which invoice we mean.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have managed five credit officers for seven years and am steady at the job, though I use AI only now and then to simplify a letter. My partner works full time at a vocational school, we have two children at school and a mortgage, and three months of expenses saved; the bills fit, but there isn't much spare after the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I'll keep checking each disputed invoice against the customer's original order and use AI only for a first draft of the plain reminder. In the first year of the plateau, we'll continue our 90 monthly extra mortgage payment if both wages hold and I'll keep the weekly call with the oldest unpaid accounts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about keeping my role, with a little unease about customers who cannot pay on the date our system wants. Our own payment is covered for now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which invoice caused trouble this week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A bakery owner had paid half a delivery, but the reminder showed the whole balance because the credit wasn't posted yet. Officer Maja checked the bank receipt while I called the owner and stopped the second letter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you let AI send reminders automatically?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not on a disputed account. I'd need a trial that catches partial payments before I let any tool press send, and I'd still give someone a number to call.

say: I'd use a **clearer reminder** if it avoids needless calls.
I'd keep the **original invoice** visible so customers know what they are being asked to pay.
think: Three months saved and two wages keep our **mortgage current** in a plateau.
I am **steady at credit management** after seven years and use AI occasionally for simpler letters.
do: Check **disputed invoices** against original orders and draft only simple reminders with AI.
Pay an **extra 90 monthly** toward the mortgage while both wages hold.
feel: She feels **calm** about work, with concern for customers facing a hard payment date.
S0.quote: A customer who owes money still needs to know exactly which invoice we mean.
fieldNote: Her **three-month reserve** and school wage support a calm baseline without suggesting unlimited spare cash.
A **partial-payment error** explains why she accepts drafts but rejects automatic sending on disputes.

steps.text: Check disputed invoices against original customer orders
Pay extra 90 monthly toward mortgage while both wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say Steady Disruption will write reminders, check invoices and answer routine payment questions, so we should test it on accounts with partial payments first. I would ask the staff representatives to see the error log before the company sets new collection targets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could manage more accounts with the same team, but head office might use the software to merge our two credit managers. Three months of savings and some other credit jobs nearby give me time to look, yet a pay gap would still land on our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll run a four-week trial on fifty old partial-payment cases and learn the tool's dispute screen myself, with the representatives able to see wrong letters. In the first year of disruption, if the trial catches every partial payment and the company pays for training time, I'd take the advanced course; if my manager post merges, I'd check posted credit supervisor jobs nearby and compare pay and school pickup hours before applying.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about being the manager who proves one less manager is needed. A good tool would still help customers, which is why I want the test done honestly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What result would stop your trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One letter demanding the full amount after a recorded partial payment would stop it until we found the fault. The small bakery that is short on cash cannot pay for our test mistake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why involve staff representatives?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If collection targets rise because the screen looks faster, officers need to show what happens on a disputed call. I want the people taking that call to see the rule before it reaches their pay review.

say: I'd seek a **partial-payment trial** before automating reminders and invoice checks.
I'd let **staff representatives** inspect wrong letters before collection targets change.
think: The software might merge **two manager posts**, including mine.
Three months saved and some local jobs help, but a **pay gap** still reaches our mortgage.
do: Trial **fifty old accounts** for four weeks with staff access to wrong letters.
Learn the **dispute screen**; take advanced training only if every partial payment is caught and company pays for time.
If merged, check **supervisor vacancies** for mortgage-covering pay and school pickup hours before applying.
feel: She feels **anxious** about her post while wanting a fair test for customers.
S1.quote: The small bakery that is short on cash cannot pay for our test mistake.
fieldNote: Her test uses **partial payments**, where a false full-balance demand harms a real small business.
She expects possible **manager consolidation** and makes training depend on proof and paid company time.

steps.text: Give staff representatives access to wrong letters in fifty-account trial
Learn dispute screen; take advanced course only if trial passes and company funds training time
Apply for posted credit supervisor roles if pay and school pickup fit after merger

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell customers AGI by 2028 can manage invoices and collection plans as well as our team, so the company must put an appeal route in writing before it changes the desk. I'd ask for a staffing date and a person who can stop a wrong demand.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The thinking work changes in 2028; robots around 2031 may handle warehouse deliveries later, but not extend my credit job. I think my post could go, and three months saved would not cover a drawn-out search plus the mortgage and the children's school costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll save copies of the partial-payment corrections and ask staff representatives for the written staffing date. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, I'd compare its demands with old bank receipts if employed; if cut, I'd apply to local account-support vacancies only where posted pay covers mortgage and childcare, then accept only a written offer, while checking any job-loss support eligibility before claiming.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage payment could pass while I'm still waiting for a job interview. I can organize the paperwork, but I cannot make a vacancy appear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask the bakery owner to speak?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the owner freely agrees and their account details stay private. I won't use a customer's trouble as a prop in a meeting about my job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you cut at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If my wage stops, my partner and I would pause the 90 extra mortgage payment and stop the children's paid Saturday art class, 65 a month, before touching the regular mortgage amount. I would tell the children the class can return when our income does.

say: I'd demand a **written appeal route** and a person who can stop a wrong AGI demand.
I'd tell customers **credit work** changes in 2028, before warehouse robots arrive.
think: My **credit desk** faces 2028 AGI; 2031 warehouse robots offer no delay.
Three months saved may not cover a long search, the **mortgage and school costs**.
do: Bring **partial-payment corrections** to staff representatives for a dated staffing decision now.
After 2028, compare **AGI demands** with receipts if employed; seek posted mortgage-covering work if cut.
Accept only a **written offer** covering mortgage and childcare; check support eligibility before claiming anything.
feel: She feels **anxious** about a possible long search if her wage stops.
S2.quote: The mortgage payment could pass while I'm still waiting for a job interview.
fieldNote: She protects a **customer's privacy** even while asking for staff input into AGI decisions.
The extra mortgage payment and children's art class are **conditional cuts**, triggered only if her wage stops.

steps.text: Ask staff representatives for written staffing date using partial-payment corrections
Compare AGI demands with old bank receipts after 2028 if employed
Apply after cut if posted pay covers mortgage and childcare; accept only written account-support offer
Stop 65 monthly art class only if her wage stops

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the credit team AGI by 2031 gives us five years to build appeal skills and to get a fair staffing map. I would ask head office which paid roles actually remain after automatic collections start.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years could let us finish a small home repair and grow our cash if both wages stay steady. But a debt-advice or appeals job is thinking work too, and AGI could handle much of it in 2031; robots around 2034 add no time to my desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I'd take a six-week debt-advice course offered by the community centre if its fee stays at or below 350 and the evening schedule fits the children's pickup. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I'd seek an internal dispute lead vacancy only if it exists and pays enough for our mortgage; otherwise I'd apply to nearby advice offices after checking their pay and hours, without leaving my current role for a possibility.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about spending money on a course while the children still need us at home. Five years gives me a chance to try it without making a rushed job move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a course outside the company?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The company course is about its own system; I want to know how to explain a debt plan to a person without collecting for my employer. A small fee from our training pot is worth it if I can practise on real cases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you work for less at an advice office?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the mortgage and school care still fit after the wage change. My partner and I would do the sums before I applied. A debt-advice wage still has to pay our mortgage and the care that gets our children home from school.

say: I'd seek a **staffing map** and funded roles after automatic collections begin.
I'd tell colleagues to build **appeal skills** over the five-year runway.
think: Two steady wages might let us build **cash** and finish a home repair.
Debt advice and appeals are **thinking work** exposed in 2031; 2034 robots do not delay them.
do: Take **debt-advice training** next spring only if fee stays at most 350 and pickup fits.
After 2031, seek **paid dispute vacancy** or nearby advice work only after mortgage and care costs are checked.
feel: She feels **uneasy** about a course fee, with time to make a careful change.
S3.quote: A debt-advice wage still has to pay our mortgage and the care that gets our children home from school.
fieldNote: Her course is **self-funded from training money**, with fee and evening pickup conditions.
She recognizes **advice as exposed**, so a role must be real and affordable, not just meaningful.

steps.text: Take six-week debt-advice course if fee at most 350 and evening pickup fits
Apply for internal dispute lead after 2031 only if vacancy pays mortgage
Apply to nearby advice offices if pay covers mortgage and school care, without resigning

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the team AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to put fair debt appeals into every automatic collection path. I would ask the company to publish each year's complaint corrections, not only the money collected.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll be 53 in 2036 and the children may be older, but the mortgage could remain. I could make a careful move into advice work; still, writing debt plans and hearing appeals are thinking tasks AGI could do then, and robots around 2039 don't give me more desk time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll keep reviewing disputed invoices and join our staff council's yearly check of complaint corrections. I'll also set aside one evening each month to attend the community centre's free debt-clinic observation if it accepts observers and my partner can cover home; in the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, I'd stay if a paid appeals role has real authority, or seek nearby openings while keeping my salary until a written offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel watchful rather than frightened by the distant date. Our three-month cushion still has to cover real school and mortgage costs, so I won't drift for ten years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why observe a free clinic?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A caller who owes money often brings a story no invoice shows, and I want to hear how an adviser asks without shame. I would not take on a client's case as an untrained volunteer; observation is the limit until I learn the work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you want from the annual review?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd want customers to see who corrected a wrong demand and staff to see which errors kept coming back. A collection total cannot tell us how many apologies were owed.

say: I'd seek **annual complaint corrections** and fair debt appeals through the staff council.
I'd say the decade should build **accountable collections**, not merely higher totals.
think: At **53**, children may need less care but the mortgage could remain.
Debt advice and appeals remain **thinking work** in 2036; robots around 2039 offer no desk shelter.
do: Keep **invoice reviews** and join yearly staff council check of complaint corrections.
Observe a **monthly debt clinic** if accepted and partner covers home.
After 2036, stay for **paid appeals authority**; otherwise seek nearby openings while employed until a signed offer.
feel: She feels **watchful** about the decade while remaining attentive to mortgage and school costs.
S4.quote: A collection total cannot tell us how many apologies were owed.
fieldNote: Her clinic plan is **observation only**, conditional on access and childcare rather than an assumed advisory post.
She ties future work to **paid appeal authority** and waits for a signed offer before leaving.

steps.text: Keep reviewing disputed customer invoices this year
Join yearly staff council review of complaint corrections
Observe monthly debt clinic if accepted and partner covers children
Seek nearby openings after 2036 if no paid appeal authority; keep salary until signed offer

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because an automated credit desk could lose manager posts while we still have a mortgage and school costs. A dated staffing plan, a customer appeal route, and actual paid openings that fit our family hours would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the bakery owner whether a second full-balance demand would make them answer the phone again. A wrong reminder can close the door before a fair payment plan starts.

headlineQuote: A wrong reminder can close the door before a fair payment plan starts.
portrait: At **43**, Zoe has managed a credit team for seven years and occasionally uses AI for reminder drafts.
Her **three-month cushion**, mortgage and two children make a lost manager wage serious despite a steady second income.
She tests **partial payments** before automation and seeks staff input on collection targets.
Fast AGI threatens her **credit desk**; longer runways allow debt-advice practice, though that work remains exposed.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her manager wage during a mortgage and school-cost stretch.
whatWouldHelp: A **staffing plan**, customer appeals and paid vacancies with workable family hours would help her move carefully.
